subject: Mid-quarter steering: scope trims, runway asks, QBR alignment

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-quarter steering: scope trims, runway asks, QBR alignment

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse and a few concrete asks ahead of prep for the QBR window. I want to keep this tight: one-line status, one explicit decision or ask, and ownership. We need alignment by end-of-week so the exec deck is stable.

High-level:
- OKR #1 (Latency SLO): On track for 95th p50 improvement but risk on infra allocation for NVMe nodes.
- OKR #2 (Dedicated): Seat rollout schedule is slipping ~2 weeks due to onboarding docs/QA.
- OKR #3 (Optimize): Cost-per-token improvements progressing but we need to lock the quantization plan.

Asks (please reply inline with owner + date):
1) Vanessa — confirm whether you can reassign two eng FTEs from feature lane to Dedicated rollout by 08/19 or propose an alternate mitigation.
2) Vivek — confirm NVMe node availability (approx # of nodes) and whether we can schedule a short burst next week. Reference ticket SUP-5723.
3) Naomi — attach a one-page risk matrix and call out top 3 decision points to include in the deck by 08/14.
4) Laura — coordinate with CS to lock customer-facing QBR dates (Prism Health) and draft the customer agenda; put a stub deck in the drive.

I've attached a QBR_prep_template.md and a short outline in the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

Short replies only please — we will consolidate and publish an updated action list on Friday.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Michael — noted. Short answers:
- FTEs: I can free up 1.5 FTEs (senior SWE + half-time PM) by 08/19, not two full FTEs without pushing a small feature out (Feature X).
- Mitigation: propose trimming the Dedicated rollout scope (defer region-burst support) which buys 3 weeks of runway. If we accept that, we can keep latency work on schedule.

I uploaded a short runway plan (runway_plan.xlsx) with two scenarios (trim scope vs pull FTEs). See tab 'Scenario B'. Drive link above.

Adding the risk matrix — top items and recommended callouts for the exec QBR:
1) NVMe allocation shortage — Impact: high; Likelihood: medium-high; Mitigation: accept scope trim for region-burst or enable temporary cloud-burst (cost delta estimated in runway_plan.xlsx).
2) Onboarding QA for Dedicated seats — Impact: medium; Likelihood: medium; Mitigation: prioritized test plan + one-week dedicated QA sprint (owner: Vanessa).
3) Quantization regression risk — Impact: medium-high; Likelihood: medium; Mitigation: lock quant profile and schedule 48-hour rollback window on canary.

Michael —

Quick infra update:
- NVMe nodes: we have capacity to provision up to 6 additional NVMe-backed inference nodes, but it requires a short maintenance window and procurement of transient burst licensing. I can schedule the maintenance for 08/18-08/19 if the team signs off.
- Ticket: SUP-5723 is the tracking ticket (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-5723). I added estimated cost delta and rollback steps in the ticket.

Request: If we proceed with the NVMe burst, can product commit to deferring the less-critical model tuning sprint (Quant Sprint 2) to after the rollouts? That reduces risk and keeps the latency SLO timeline cleaner.

Vivek
VP Infra Engineering
